title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & The ₹100 Revenue Waterfall
book_title: Chapter 3: Logistics, Fluorspar Sourcing & Where Every ₹100 of Sales Goes

epigraph.quote: In hazardous chemistry, your logistics fleet and raw-material port access are as much a moat as your reactor.
epigraph.author: Chemical Supply Chain Rule

web_blocks.html: Tanfac sells strictly B2B industrial direct. It has no retail dealers, middlemen, or consumer channels [2][10]. The company serves over 100 domestic and global industrial buyers across farm chemicals, drugs, solar PV, aluminium, and fluorochemicals [10]. Its off-take splits into two tracks. Part of its AHF and Potassium Fluoride goes to co-promoter Anupam Rasayan India Limited as a captive fluorination input [4][10]. Under Ind AS 24 related-party rules, these deals run at arm's length in the normal course of business with Audit Committee approval [4][10]. The rest goes to third-party domestic contracts and export buyers [4][10].

Anhydrous Hydrofluoric Acid is toxic, fuming, and corrosive, so shipping it is a tough engineering moat on its own [26]. Tanfac's SIPCOT Cuddalore plant sits along Tamil Nadu's coast near Cuddalore Port and deep-water hubs at Karaikal, Chennai, and Ennore [10][26]. Domestic loads travel in lined road tankers made with rubber, HDPE, or special alloys [26]. Each tanker carries pressure-relief valves, shut-off valves, and GPS tracking [26]. Export loads of HF and derivatives move in T14-rated lined ISO tank containers that meet International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) rules [26]. This hazmat fleet builds a strong regional moat. Foreign rivals cannot cheaply ship liquid AHF into southern India without ISO tank fleets and port permits.

On the inbound side lies Tanfac's biggest supply risk: 100% import reliance for acid-grade fluorspar [15]. India lacks commercial reserves of high-grade fluorite [15]. Local HF makers must import acid-spar from China, South Africa, Morocco, Thailand, and Vietnam [15]. Tanfac spreads orders across Africa and Southeast Asia and runs a ~100,000 MTPA captive sulphuric acid plant on-site [4][15]. Still, landed fluorspar costs swing with Chinese export quotas, ocean freight, and USD/INR rates [4][15]. Working capital also shifted sharply in FY2026. Debtor Days improved from 65 to 57 days, and Inventory Days fell from 112 to 79 days [1]. Yet Days Payable shrank from 48 days to just 21 days [1]. That pushed the Cash Conversion Cycle to 115 days (versus 43 days in FY2022) and pulled CFO-to-EBITDA down [1].

web_blocks.html: Governance over captive sales also needs close watch in Chapter 3. Co-promoter Anupam Rasayan is both a lead owner and a buyer of AHF and Potassium Fluoride [4][10]. Tanfac's Audit Committee approves these deals in advance and logs them under Ind AS 24 as normal, arm's-length trades [4][10]. Outside investors must check those annual Ind AS 24 tables to confirm captive volume never hurts transfer margins. Meanwhile, the FY2026 waterfall shows why working-capital control matters so much. Paying vendors in 21 days while collecting from clients in 57 days leaves a 36-day net credit gap, even before counting 79 days of fluorspar and finished stock [1].

Cost Structure Sensitivity & Raw-Material Pass-Through Lag: The FY2026 waterfall proves that raw materials drive Tanfac's cost base. Cost of Materials Consumed hit ₹453.47 crore, or 63.78% of sales [1][5]. Employee Benefits Expense was just ₹27.63 crore, or 3.89% of sales [1][5]. Other Operating Expenses—power, fuel, stores, repairs, and freight—took ₹115.90 crore, or 16.30% of sales [1][5]. Comparing FY2025 against FY2026 shows how raw-material timing swings operating leverage. In FY2025, materials cost ₹307.60 crore on ₹557 crore sales (55.2% of sales), letting OPM hit 24% [1][5]. In FY2026, materials jumped to 63.78% of sales—an 858 basis-point gross-margin drop [1][5]. That shift explains why OPM fell from 24% to 16%, even as payroll fell from 4.1% to 3.9% of sales [1][5].

Freight, Port Handling & Working Capital Mechanics: Acid-grade fluorspar arrives in bulk ships from China, South Africa, Morocco, Thailand, and Vietnam [15]. To guard against shipping delays, Tanfac holds large ore stocks at Cuddalore [15]. Inventory Days stood at 112 days in FY2025 before easing to 79 days in FY2026 [1]. At the same time, growing merchant and export sales stretched Debtor Days from 28 days (FY2022) to 57–65 days (FY2025–FY2026) [1]. Meanwhile, Days Payable fell steeply from 77 days (FY2024) to 21 days (FY2026) [1]. That 56-day drop in vendor credit explains nearly all of the 115-day Cash Conversion Cycle and the gap between ₹70 crore PAT and ₹43 crore operating cash flow [1].

book_paragraphs: To see why nobody builds a hydrofluoric acid plant next to an office park, watch one load leave Tanfac's Cuddalore gate. Workers are not strapping boxes onto a flatbed truck. They are pumping fuming, tissue-burning acid into a lined road tanker with pressure valves, shut-off lines, and GPS tracking. Or they are filling a T14-rated lined ISO tank bound for Karaikal, Chennai, or Cuddalore Port under strict sea-freight rules.

That hazmat reality defines Tanfac's sales moat. The firm sells direct to over 100 industrial B2B buyers—farm chemical plants, drug makers, solar fabs, and aluminium smelters—with zero middlemen. Part of that output flows to co-promoter Anupam Rasayan on an arm's-length, Audit-Committee-checked basis. That tie gives Tanfac a steady anchor buyer for AHF and Potassium Fluoride, while the rest serves third-party local and export clients. Shipping liquid HF across oceans in ISO tanks is costly and tightly policed. Buyers in southern and western India therefore face high friction if they try to swap Tanfac for an overseas vendor.

Now walk over to the inbound gate at Cuddalore, and that moat flips into a risk. India has almost no commercial mines for acid-grade fluorspar. Every tonne of fluorite feeding Tanfac's kilns arrives by ship from China, South Africa, Morocco, Thailand, or Vietnam. Tanfac cuts single-country risk by buying across Africa and Southeast Asia, and makes up to 100,000 tonnes of captive sulphuric acid on-site. Even so, it cannot dodge global ore price cycles, ocean freight spikes, or dollar-rupee swings.

Let us trace every ₹100 that entered Tanfac's till in FY2026, when audited sales hit ₹711 crore. Right off the top, ₹63.78 went straight out to buy raw materials—mainly fluorspar, sulphur, and potassium salts—totaling ₹453.47 crore. Payroll took a lean ₹3.89 (₹27.63 crore). Power, fuel, repairs, and other plant overheads took ₹16.30 (₹115.90 crore). That left ₹16.03 in Operating EBITDA, or ₹114 crore.

Below the operating line, depreciation took ₹2.39 (₹17 crore), up 70% from FY2025 as new AHF and Solar DHF lines started up. Interest took ₹0.84 (₹6 crore), other income added ₹0.28 (₹2 crore), and taxes took ₹3.23 (₹23 crore). That left ₹9.85 in net profit, or ₹70 crore. Then comes the cash-flow check: vendor payable days shrank from 48 days to just 21 days. Working capital absorbed cash, leaving only ₹6.05 per ₹100 (₹43 crore) in operating cash flow. After spending ₹11.53 per ₹100 (₹82 crore) on capex, Tanfac posted negative Free Cash Flow of -₹5.49 per ₹100 (-₹39 crore). That is the classic cash profile of a chemical plant mid-expansion.

Step back and look at Cuddalore on a map of southern India. Sitting right along the Bay of Bengal, Tanfac's SIPCOT site is minutes from Cuddalore Port and close to deep-water hubs at Karaikal, Chennai, and Ennore. The company imports 100% of its fluorspar and sulphur by sea, and exports more chemicals in T14 ISO tanks to global buyers like Japan. That coastal pin saves heavy inland rail and truck freight every year.

The working-capital math in the FY2026 waterfall also earns a second look. Collecting from buyers in 57 days while paying raw-material vendors in 21 days—down from 77 days two years prior—creates a 36-day credit gap. On top of that sits 79 days of ore and chemical stock. That 115-day Cash Conversion Cycle explains why ₹114 crore of EBITDA yielded just ₹43 crore of operating cash flow in FY2026. Reversing even half of that payable squeeze would free up tens of crores in internal cash.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Look closely at the FY2026 ₹100 waterfall: ₹63.78 goes to raw materials, ₹9.85 becomes accounting profit, ₹6.05 turns into operating cash, and ₹11.53 goes right back into capex. When a chemical firm is mid-build, reported profit is only half the picture. Working capital and capex decide how much cash stays inside.

book_subsections.title: The Supplier-Credit Squeeze in Working Capital
paragraphs: One sharp forensic clue stands out in Tanfac's FY2026 ratios. Debtor Days improved from 65 to 57 days, and Inventory Days fell from 112 to 79 days. Yet Days Payable fell from 77 days in FY2024 to 48 days in FY2025 and just 21 days in FY2026. Paying ore and sulphur vendors faster pushed the Cash Conversion Cycle to 115 days and pulled CFO-to-EBITDA down to 56%. Watching if payable terms ease in FY2027 will show how much buying power Tanfac holds.

At the same time, note how lean the fixed payroll is: staff costs took under 4% of FY2026 sales (₹27.63 crore on ₹711 crore). Profit swings at Cuddalore come from raw-material spreads and plant load, not headcount.

book_subsections.title: Captive vs. Merchant Off-Take Balance
paragraphs: Having Anupam Rasayan as co-promoter and anchor buyer lowers volume risk in slow merchant cycles. Yet minority investors must check annual Ind AS 24 tables to ensure AHF and Potassium Fluoride transfer prices stay strictly arm's-length.

book_subsections.title: Why an 858-Basis-Point Raw Material Shift Swamped Operating Leverage
paragraphs: Compare Tanfac's audited FY2025 and FY2026 filings side by side, and one number jumps out. In FY2025, raw materials took ₹307.60 crore on ₹557 crore of sales—roughly 55.2% of revenue. In FY2026, raw materials took ₹453.47 crore on ₹711 crore of sales—nearly 63.8% of revenue. That 858-basis-point jump in material cost swamped volume gains and lean 3.9% payroll costs, pulling operating margins down from 24% to 16%.

That is the daily reality of buying 100% imported fluorspar and sulphur on global markets while selling into B2B contracts that reset with a lag. When ore or sulphur spikes—or when acid prices cool faster than ore deals reset—gross margins take the hit first. Tracking that material-to-sales ratio each quarter is the cleanest way to gauge real-time pricing power.
